summary.text: Uniswap is a trading system that uses pools of tokens to let people swap directly from their wallets, according to Uniswap Labs.
The web app, wallet and developer tools come from Uniswap Labs, which also helps develop the trading system.
People who hold UNI can vote on fees and other settings, according to Uniswap Labs.
The apps connect traders to shared pools, and some trades use competing providers to fill signed orders, the project says.
Callers give up UNI to withdraw collected trading fees, and the submitted UNI goes to a burn address, the project says.
The app also sends Earn deposits to lending vaults, where borrowers pay the interest depositors receive, the project says.
The web app has no interface fee, while pool fees and blockchain transaction costs can still apply, according to Uniswap Labs.
Uniswap Labs reports that some newer pools collect protocol fees, although its token guide still lists fees only for older pools.

differs.why: CoinGecko’s November 23 estimate used different accounting from Ethereum’s totalSupply() getter. The approximate match after excluding the configured recipient suggests burn accounting. The tracker’s precise exclusions and timestamp remain unverified.

The token guide limits active fees to v2 and v3, while the November governance post includes v4. Ethereum’s configured controller supports the v4 rollout, but the individual pools and other chains were outside the chain check.
